This is a unique program for graduate students at Stony Brook University that provides them the opportunity to develop and apply their experiences and knowledge from both inside and outside the classroom to the Residential Community. The Assistant Coordinators within our program work collaboratively with the professional staff to develop student staff, participate in department and University functions, and contribute to the creation of an on-campus living environment conducive to student success. Campus Residences is an exciting, fast-paced environment; ideal candidates must be flexible, team-oriented, and passionate about student development.

events.title: Systematic Review Incubator – Apply Now!
events.description:
Interested in conducting a systematic or scoping review but not sure where to start? Have an idea for a review but need structure, support, and accountability to see it through?

Apply for the Systematic Review Incubator, a structured, cohort-based program designed to guide participants through the evidence synthesis process. With guidance from librarians with expertise in evidence synthesis, participants will work through the stages of the review process, from developing a research question and protocol to building comprehensive searches, screening studies, and synthesizing data. Participants can complete the initial five-month phase with a registered protocol and the foundational materials needed to conduct their review, or continue for up to 12 months to work toward a high-quality, submission-ready manuscript that follows established evidence synthesis methods and reporting guidelines.

The program is open to members of the Stony Brook community, including students, faculty, clinicians, and staff. Undergraduate students must be in their junior year or above.

Our goal is for all of us to become more confident and equipped with the Word to share the Gospel with those around us.
